title: Fruit and vegetable sorting cards
subject: Art & Design
unit: Summer 2: Sky painting and food (Splendid Skies and Chop, Slice & Mash)
source: Written for art/y1 lesson 11 (Fruit and vegetable sorting cards (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 11: Where fruit and vegetables come from. Listen, look, then do the tasks with a grown-up.

blocks.answer: Fruit: apple, banana, orange, pear, grapes. Vegetables: carrot, broccoli, potato, onion.

blocks.title: Sort into: On a tree / On a plant / Under the ground
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: On a tree, On a plant, Under the ground.
blocks.answer: On a tree: apple; orange. On a plant: strawberry; peas. Under the ground: carrot; potato

keywords.def: the part of a plant that holds the seeds
another part of a plant we eat, like a root or leaf
the part of a plant under the ground

questions.q: Which part of a lettuce do we eat?
Give one word to describe an orange.
questions.a: For example: juicy, round or sweet

questions.q: Core: Sort six picture cards into on a tree, on a plant and under the ground.
questions.a: Tree: apple, orange; plant: strawberry, peas; under the ground: carrot, potato

questions.q: Extend: Taste one fruit or vegetable at home and write two describing words.
Stretch: Is a tomato a fruit? How do you know?

questions.a: B) Under the ground. A carrot is a root, so it grows under the ground.

questions.q: Big question: where did your apple grow?
